text.p: The mark was weak-toned in late Europe as the market digested a slowdown in German money supply growth and the dollar held firm.
German M3 growth slowed to 8.0 percent in November from October's 8.4, the Bundesbank said. The bank's target range for M3 is four to seven percent.

The German central bank surprised the market with a generous liquidity injection, and that -- combined with recent rate cuts by France and Sweden -- sparked some quiet speculation that the Bundesbank just might move on rates at Thursday's council meeting -- its last of 1996.

"I'd be very surprised (if the Bundesbank cut). The only thing that gives you a slight nag is the fact we've had France and a couple of other countries move -- it has been suggested that perhaps there are some concerted ideas around," said Peter Wood at Bank of Boston.
"But I'd be very, very surprised given what the Bundesbank monthly report said," he added.
In its December report, the bank said M3 growth might exceed its target at the end of this year. The pace of monetary expansion had accelerated somewhat in recent months, it said.
The mark eased to 984.25/75 Italian lire and 84.19/20 pesetas by 1506 GMT from late Tuesday's 986.20/55 and 84.21/24.

The French franc failed to make headway, softening to 3.3793/98 per mark from late yesterday's 3.3760/64 as a lowering of French call money boosted speculation more official interest rate reductions were in the pipeline.
The Bank of France yesterday shaved its intervention rate to 3.15 percent from 3.20 and its five-to-10 day lending rate to 4.60 percent from 4.75.

Elsewhere, the mark powered to fresh 30-month highs against the Swiss franc. Mark/Swiss hit 85.66 centimes before settling at 85.61/63 by 1512 GMT, up from Tuesday's European close around 85.47/48. -- Abigail Levene +44-171-542-8968
